scores.evidence: metrics.json has no hard failures: overflowX false, 0 console, mermaid, unknown-block and broken-image errors. Both diagrams (Figure 1 on mobile-jp-04, Figure 2 on mobile-jp-12/13) use top-down layouts with short Japanese labels that are readable at 390 px. The term tables, code blocks, steps, prompt, checklist and flashcards all render cleanly on desktop and mobile. No privacy data appears on any screen.

textOnlyScreens is empty on desktop and mobile. Every screen holds a table, figure, code, steps or a check. Desktop JP median is 39 chars per line (target 30-40; max 56 on one line). The code blocks are pre-wrapped to short lines, so the SKILL.md and researcher.md files fit within 390 px without side-scrolling (mobile-jp-06, -14, -23).

The lesson is Japanese-only and all visible text is Japanese. English appears only as parenthetical terms (skill, frontmatter, progressive disclosure, subagent, fork) and as code. Contrast is good throughout, the callouts (info and the red 'よくある失敗' box) are legible, and no controls sit under the top or bottom bars on any mobile screen.

niceToHave: Practice section heading '演習：自分の手順をスキルにし、調べものを任せる' breaks as 'スキルに / し、' at 390 px (pages/mobile-jp-18.png). A shorter heading, or a break after 'スキルにし、', would read more naturally.
reader: the end banner says 'このコースの最後のレッスンまで読み終えました。' because drafts are not listed in course.json (pages/mobile-jp-31.png, pages/desktop-jp-21.png). This is known behaviour.
reader: inline code such as 'disable-model-invocation: true' and 'deploy-prod-manual' wraps mid-token on mobile (pages/mobile-jp-09.png, -10.png, -19.png, -25.png). This is known reader behaviour.
summary: The screenshots show the lesson under review: metrics.json lessonHash sha256:d414e3e1a2e0ec5b matches the expected hash. There are no hard failures, and all 31 mobile and 21 desktop JP screens are clean: diagrams, tables, pre-wrapped code and the quiz options are readable at 390 px, with no clipping, overflow or personal data. The only finding is optional: a slightly awkward line break in the practice heading on mobile.
